findings.title: orders.customer_id has no foreign key, and two fixes already repaired orphaned orders
findings.hazard: Orders can reference a customer that no longer exists
findings.scenario: An admin deletes a customer with orders; the delete skips model callbacks, so the orders stay behind
findings.blast_radius: orders and customers; invoicing and the monthly revenue export read both
findings.trace: 1. db/schema.rb:88 declares orders.customer_id as bigint with no foreign key. 2. app/models/order.rb:8 checks belongs_to only on save through the model. 3. customers_controller.rb:42 calls delete_all, skipping dependent: :restrict_with_error on app/models/customer.rb:4. 4. Fixes 9c1d2e4 and 5b7a0f3 repaired orphaned orders by hand
findings.impact: Orders whose customer is gone break invoicing and drop out of revenue reports
findings.exposure: Core table orders; 3 writers of customer_id; fixes 9c1d2e4 and 5b7a0f3 patched orphaned rows in the window

enforcement.gaps: Only the model checks it; delete_all at customers_controller.rb:42 and raw SQL bypass it, and the schema has no constraint

findings.rollout_reason: Orphaned orders already exist, so the key cannot be validated until they are cleaned; validating it in the migration that adds it would also block writes to orders for the length of the scan
invariants: Every orders.customer_id references an existing customers.id
Deleting a customer who has orders is refused by the database, not only by the model
steps: 1. List orphaned orders with a read-only query and decide their owner (verify: the count on a staging copy is the one reported to the requester)
2. Add the foreign key as NOT VALID in its own migration (verify: the migration takes under a second on a staging copy; inserting an order for a missing customer is refused)
3. VALIDATE CONSTRAINT in a later migration once no orphan is left (verify: validation passes on a staging copy; orders and customers stay writable while it runs)
findings.fix: Clean the orphans, then add the foreign key in two migrations: NOT VALID, then VALIDATE

validation.evidence: db/schema.rb:88 has no add_foreign_key for orders; customers_controller.rb:42 calls delete_all; git show 9c1d2e4 5b7a0f3 updates orders with missing customers

findings.title: Customer merge deletes the duplicate before moving its orders, with no transaction
findings.hazard: A failure between the delete and the move leaves orders orphaned
findings.scenario: The job is retried on any error (config/sidekiq.yml:4); a timeout after the delete repeats nothing useful
findings.trace: 1. merge_customers_job.rb:22 deletes the duplicate customer. 2. :28 then moves its orders to the kept customer. 3. No transaction wraps the two writes
findings.impact: Orders of a merged customer point at a deleted row; once F-001 adds the foreign key, the job fails halfway instead
findings.exposure: Core tables customers and orders; the job runs nightly over every flagged duplicate

enforcement.gaps: The model refuses deleting a customer with orders, but the job calls delete, which skips that check

invariants: After a merge, every order of the duplicate belongs to the kept customer
A merge that fails at any step leaves both customers and all orders as they were
steps: 1. Wrap the move and the delete in one transaction, moving the orders first (verify: job spec green; a raise between the two writes leaves both customers and their orders unchanged)
2. Make the job skip a duplicate that is already gone (verify: running the job twice on the same pair changes nothing the second time)
findings.fix: One transaction, orders moved before the duplicate is deleted

validation.evidence: app/jobs/merge_customers_job.rb:22 Customer.where(id: dup).delete_all runs before :28; no transaction block in the file

findings.title: Wallet debit reads the balance and writes it back without a lock
findings.hazard: Two concurrent debits both pass the balance check
findings.scenario: A double-clicked checkout or a retried request debits the same wallet twice at once
findings.trace: 1. debit.rb:12 reads wallet.balance. 2. :15 compares it with the amount. 3. :18 saves balance - amount, with no row lock or version column
findings.impact: The balance goes below zero, or one of two debits is lost
findings.exposure: Core table wallets (money); 2 writers of wallets.balance; no fix commit in the window

enforcement.gaps: The model validates balance >= 0 on the value it read; nothing in the schema stops a racing write

invariants: Two concurrent debits of 30 from a balance of 50 leave 20 and one refused debit
steps: 1. Load the wallet with a row lock inside the debit transaction (verify: wallet spec green; two threads debiting 30 from 50 leave 20 and one refusal)
findings.fix: Lock the wallet row for the read-check-write, then add a check constraint when the area is next touched

validation.evidence: app/services/wallet/debit.rb:12-18 reads and saves without lock or lock_version; db/schema.rb:61 has no check on balance

findings.title: audit_events uses an integer primary key, against the bigint rule
findings.hazard: The id sequence runs out at about 2.1 billion
findings.scenario: audit_events grows by about 40 million rows a month
findings.blast_radius: 1 table; the audit log, which nothing else references
findings.trace: 1. The migration at :3 creates audit_events with id: :integer. 2. db/schema.rb:12 shows the integer key. 3. docs/ops/capacity.md:14 records 38% of the range in use
findings.impact: Inserts into audit_events fail once the sequence passes the integer range
findings.exposure: Non-core table; 38% of the id range used (docs/ops/capacity.md:14)

enforcement.gaps: Nothing guards the integer range: the schema declares the key integer, and no check or alert watches the sequence's headroom

findings.rollout_reason: Changing the key to bigint rewrites audit_events under an exclusive lock; at its size that blocks audit writes for minutes
steps: 1. In a maintenance window, change audit_events.id and its sequence to bigint (verify: on a staging copy the rewrite finishes within the window and inserts resume)
findings.fix: Widen the key to bigint in a scheduled window, as ADR 0011 requires

findings.title: legacy_exports table has no primary key
findings.scenario: Nothing writes or reads the table
findings.trace: 1. The migration at :2 creates legacy_exports with id: false. 2. No model, query or job names it
findings.impact: A table nothing writes cannot be corrupted
findings.fix: Hand to prune-scan as a removal candidate

validation.evidence: db/migrate/20190405090000_create_legacy_exports.rb:2 is the only mention; a search for legacy_exports in app/ and lib/ returns 0
